title: Greetings and goodbyes
subtitle: 인사
review: Written by Claude. The Korean and the romanization have not been checked by a Korean speaker. No audio yet: the Korean voice is not chosen. Burmese lines and the Korean category headings drafted by Claude. Check them before publishing.

categories.desc: Hello at any time of day, meeting someone new, and catching up.
cards:
안녕하세요.
မင်္ဂလာပါ။

Morning, afternoon or evening. To friends: Annyeong.

만나서 반갑습니다.
တွေ့ရတာ ဝမ်းသာပါတယ်။

Only the first time you meet someone.
Pleased to meet you. / I'm in your care.

잘 부탁드립니다.
ခင်ခင်မင်မင် ဆက်ဆံပေးပါ။

오랜만이에요.
မတွေ့တာ ကြာပြီနော်။

잘 지내요?
နေကောင်းလား။

categories.desc: Thank you, you're welcome, sorry, and how to call a waiter.
cards:
감사합니다.
ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်။

A little softer and friendlier: Gomawoyo.

아니에요.
ရပါတယ်။

Literally 'no': the usual modest answer to thanks.

죄송합니다.
တောင်းပန်ပါတယ်။

저기요.
တဆိတ်လောက်။

To call a waiter, or to stop someone in the street.

categories.desc: Who leaves and who stays, the end of the workday, and good night.
cards:
안녕히 가세요.
ကောင်းကောင်းသွားပါ။

Said by the person who stays: 'go in peace'.
Goodbye. (when you are the one leaving)

안녕히 계세요.
ကောင်းကောင်းနေခဲ့ပါ။

Said by the person who leaves: 'stay in peace'.

또 봐요.
နောက်မှ တွေ့မယ်။

수고하셨습니다.
ပင်ပန်းသွားပြီနော်။

Said to colleagues at the end of the day.

안녕히 주무세요.
ကောင်းကောင်းအိပ်ပါ။

Polite. To friends: Jal ja.
